entries.def:
πτέρυξ, -υγος, ἡ
(πέτομαι), [in LXX chiefly for כָּנָף ;] 
a wing: of birds, Mat.23.37, Luk.13.34, Rev.12.14; of creatures seen in a vision, Rev.4.8; 9.9.†
(AS)

πτηνός, -ή, -όν
(πέτομαι), [in Aq.: Job.5.7 * ;] 
winged; as subst., π., birds: 1Co.15.39.†
(AS)

πτοέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX chiefly for חָתַת ni. ;] 
to terrify. Pass., to be terrified: Luk.21.9; 24.37 (WH, mg., θροηθέντες).†
(AS)

πτόησις, -εως, ἡ
(πτοέω) [in LXX: Pro.3.25 (פַּחַד), Sir.50.4 א1, 1Ma.3.25 R * ;] 
a fluttering, excitement, caused by any emotion, but esp. by fear, hence, terror: φοβεῖσθαι πτόησιν, to be afraid with (cogn. accusative) or of any terror (see ICC, in l): 1Pe.3.6.†
(AS)

Πτολεμαΐς, -ΐδος, ἡ 
Ptolemais, a maritime city of Phœnicea: Act.21.7.†
(AS)

πτύον, -ου, τό 
[in Sm.: Isa.30.24 * ;] 
a winnowing shovel or fan: Mat.3.12, Luk.3.17.†
(AS)

πτύρομαι depon., 
to be startled, frightened: Php.1.28. (The active πτύρω is also found in some late writers.) †
(AS)

πτύσμα, -τος, τό,
(πτύω) 
spittle: Jhn.9.6 (Hipp., Polyb., al.).†
(AS)

πτύσσω 
to fold; of a scroll, to roll up: βιβλίον, Luk.4.20 (cf. ἀνα-πτύσσω).†
(AS)

πτύω 
[in LXX: Num.12.14 (יָרָק), Sir.28.12 * ;] 
to spit: Mrk.7.33; 8.23, Jhn.9.6 (cf. ἐκ-, ἐμ-πτύω).†
(AS)
